title: The inner shape of the actions and outcome columns of a hand-over decision entry is not in any source
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.31; legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 7 and 11
description: TSD P7 T3.1 types decision_log_entry.actions and decision_log_entry.outcome as jsonb with 'Workbench' as the source and gives no element list. Neither FSD P7 v3 nor the legacy story says how the 16 EFS history items and the created-or-linked result are carried on the entry, so a criterion cannot assert the inner shape and the tests can only assert counts, source system and action codes.
evidence: TSD P7 T3.1 rows DF-DEC-014 (actions, jsonb) and DF-DEC-015 (outcome, jsonb) carry no element list; FSD P7 v3 A2.2 names the fields of an entry and not the content of these two; legacy RWB-E2-001 AC1 asserts the 16 interaction entries and the business date only.
owner_role: Solution architect with the data steward
proposed: Add the element list of both columns to the DecisionLogEntry resource of RWB-P7-E2005-CON and to the record shape of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON at the contract review; until then the story writes the history items in a fixed order and the tests assert the counts, the source system and the action codes.

title: Where the R-UNI-40 repeat count of a hand-over record is kept and reported is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-001 AC2, BR6 and section 4; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; TSD P7 v2 T3.1
description: The legacy story requires that a repeat hand-over is ignored and counted, and AC2 shows the count in the run summary of the hand-over job. In the target the entry is sealed here while the run summary is rwb-integration's, and no source names a column, a counter or a read that carries the repeat count between the two services.
evidence: Legacy section 7 AC2 reads 'the run summary shows 1 repeat for "A-0001"'; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-03 reads 'adds 1 to the repeat count for R-UNI-40'; TSD P7 T3.1 has no counter column on decision_log_entry or approval.
proposed: Keep the count as a meter of rwb-decision, exposed on the operational dashboard of the service and returned in the response header of the record submission, and have the run summary of rwb-integration read it; confirm the mechanism at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2001-CON.

title: No source fixes the query parameters and paging of GET /decision-log
source: Ownership Map v1, P7 provided operations; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1; TSD P7 v2 T3.1
description: The Ownership Map lists GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} under P7 and no source gives the query parameters, the paging shape, the default order or the maximum page of the list read. The legacy story read the timeline with GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline and query parameters type, from and to, which is a case service path in the target.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 P7 row lists the two paths with no parameter contract; TSD P7 T-A.1 lists API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 with the path and the access only; legacy RWB-E2-001 section 12 lists GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline with Query: type, from, to.
proposed: Fix the parameters caseId, decision, ruleId, ruleVersion, approver, from, to, page and size and a page size of 1 to 500 in RWB-P7-E2005-CON, in the order of decided_at, and let RWB-P7-E2005-APP implement and test them.

title: The five-minute ledger completeness target has no named alert, owner or threshold
source: Architecture v5 slide 20 notes; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03; TSD P7 v2 T7
description: Architecture v5 sets a five-minute target for rwb-decision to read rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger and names gap alerts and chain verification, and no source gives the alert message, the role that receives it, the lag at which it fires or the period over which it is measured. The story therefore states the target and writes no alert of its own.
evidence: Architecture v5 extract reads 'rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes' and 'a 5-minute completeness target, gap alerts and chain verification'; TSD P7 T7 has NFR-033 to NFR-038 and NFR-076 to NFR-078 with no ingest-lag row.
owner_role: Platform observability owner with the P7 solution architect
proposed: Register the ingest lag as a metric of RWB-PLT-OBS with the threshold as a parameter, raise the gap alert to RW-PLATADM under RWB-P7-E1027-APP, and keep this story to the sealed entry.

title: The legacy story puts the EFS history append in the decision module while the Ownership Map and DP-18 put the interaction ledger in rwb-source-data
source: Legacy RWB-E2-001 sections 4, 5, 11 and 12; Ownership Map v1, P1 and P7 rows; Template and Rules R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-18
description: The legacy contract declares InteractionLedger.appendEfsHistory under recovery.decision.api and writes 16 interaction entries from the hand-over step, which fits the modular monolith. The Ownership Map gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data, DP-18 records the same default ruling, and the P7 owned tables hold no interaction table. This story therefore records the history items on the entry and writes no ledger row.
evidence: Legacy section 12 reads '// P7 recovery.decision.api int InteractionLedger.appendEfsHistory(...)'; legacy section 11 lists DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-013 as interaction writes; the Ownership Map lists the six P7 tables with no interaction table and the P1 rows hold the ledger; Template and Rules R3 gives the interaction ledger to P1 rwb-source-data.
owner_role: Solution architect and the Ownership Map owner
proposed: Keep the ledger with rwb-source-data as DP-18 records it, keep the history items of the hand-over on the P7 entry as evidence, and record the move in the Change Register.

title: The exact LOV-DECISION value of the hand-over entry is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E2-001 metadata row Decision; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 T3-like field note
description: The legacy story names the decision as 'D6 entry' and TSD P7 types decision_code as a varchar(8) LOV of D5.1 to D9.3 plus the access events. No source states whether the hand-over entry carries D6 or a sub-code of D6, so the criteria name 'D6' as the legacy story does and the list value is read as data.
evidence: Legacy metadata row reads 'Decision | D6 entry'; FSD P7 v3 decision_log_entry.decision_code reads 'D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7, or an access event'; TSD P7 T3.2 LOV list is not printed for LOV-DECISION.
proposed: Confirm the value with RW-COE when the LOV-DECISION rows are loaded, and read it as a reference row so a correction is a data change and not a release.

title: The story line carries one C row and no H row while the pattern table adds six platform H rows and the guard
source: Work Package B2-P7-017 story line; Template and Rules R5.5 DP table and R5.7 lane rules; Ownership Map v1
description: The story line fixes H empty and one C row, RWB-P2-E2001-CON. DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 each add a platform H row, the two reads are guarded by DP-08, and the record shape is fixed by RWB-P7-E2005-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; all of them are named in the story and none is carried in the metadata table. Because each added H row is a platform CON story, the lane still starts on Day 1.
evidence: Story line of WP B2-P7-017: H [], C [RWB-P2-E2001-CON]; Template and Rules R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19; R5.7 rule 3 allows H only to the same service or a platform CON story.
owner_role: Coordinator of the realignment with the P7 solution architect
proposed: Carry the six platform CON rows and RWB-P7-E2005-CON in the dependency map of the assembled story set, and keep the lane at Day 1 because every added H row is a platform contract.
